title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Monthly Maintenance and Paper Statement Charges
content:
Two periodic charges can fall on a Savings & Money Market Accounts product when its statement cycle closes: the monthly maintenance fee and the paper statement fee. This page states when each is due and when the maintenance fee is set aside.

## Maintenance fee

**When it is charged.** As each statement cycle closes, the account is charged its tier's monthly maintenance fee, once, as a maintenance charge belonging to that cycle, unless the account satisfies at least one of the waivers its tier offers for that cycle. The tier that counts is the one the account is on when the cycle closes.

**How the waivers work.** The waivers are alternatives: meeting any single one is enough. The fee is either charged in full or not at all; it is never cut down in proportion or partly excused. A waiver that the tier marks as not offered cannot be relied on.

**The waivers available, where the tier offers them:**
- the lowest end-of-day balance on any day of the cycle is at or above the tier's minimum daily balance level;
- the automatic transfers from checking that posted in the cycle add up to at least the tier's automatic transfer level;
- the owner, when the cycle closes, is younger than the tier's waiver age;
- when the cycle closes, the same customer has an active Personal Checking account of one of the tier's linked checking tiers;
- the customer's relationship balance when the cycle closes, measured the way Personal Checking measures its relationship balance but leaving out any mortgage principal, is at or above the tier's relationship balance level.

**When it is never charged.**
- For the cycle during which the account was opened.
- On an account whose status is anything other than active at the close of the cycle; the account's status on the bank's records is what decides this.
- A second time: an account bears at most one maintenance fee per statement cycle, judged from the charges already on its ledger for that cycle.

## Paper statement fee

If the account's statement delivery method is paper when the cycle closes, the tier's paper statement fee is charged for that cycle, unless the owner has reached the tier's exemption age by that close. The delivery method in force at close is what counts, so a change of delivery method made during the cycle decides the charge only if it is still in force when the cycle closes.

A tier figure of 0.00 for either charge means no charge is posted at all.

## Truth cases (hypothetical Statement Savings cycles, active at close, not the opening cycle)

| Lowest daily balance at or above the level | Automatic transfers reach the level | Active linked checking of a listed tier | Maintenance fee charged |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | no | no |
| no | yes | no | no |
| no | no | yes | no |
| no | no | no | yes, in full |

## Points of judgement

**The account was dormant when the cycle closed. Is a maintenance fee due?** No; the fee applies only to an account active at close.

**The lowest balance missed the level by one cent, but an automatic transfer met its level. Is the fee reduced or waived?** Waived entirely, because one waiver is enough.
